subject: Biotechnology
title: Biological Logic Gates
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biological Logic Gates usable.

hook.text: AND, OR, NOT — silicon computers use logic gates, and so can living cells. Biological computing is real.

buildup.text: Genetic circuits use promoters as inputs and fluorescent proteins as outputs — if two signals are present, the cell glows.

discovery.text: MIT's 2019 cell computer performed 12-bit computation inside E. coli — the most complex genetic logic circuit ever built.

twist.text: Biological circuits are noisy — molecular fluctuations cause errors that silicon transistors would never make.

climax.text: CRISPR-based logic gates store computation results in DNA — permanent records of cellular decisions written into the genome.

punchline.text: Cells that compute — biological logic gates process information inside living organisms.

quiz.question: What is a key disadvantage of biological logic gates compared to silicon?
options: They cannot perform AND or OR operations
Molecular noise causes errors that silicon transistors would not make, reducing computational reliability
They require external electricity to function

details.summary: Biological logic gates are genetic circuits that perform Boolean operations inside living cells, processing molecular inputs through AND, OR, NOT, and other logical functions. They enable cells to make complex decisions based on combinations of environmental signals.
details.whyItMatters: Programming cells with logic enables sophisticated therapeutic and industrial applications. Cancer-killing cells that activate only when detecting multiple tumor markers, or biosensors that respond to specific chemical combinations, require
takeaways: Genetic circuits can perform AND, OR, NOT, and other Boolean operations
Combining gates creates complex decision-making programs in living cells
Applications include smart therapeutics that activate under specific conditions

faq.question: How does a biological AND gate work?
faq.answer: A biological AND gate produces output only when two inputs are both present. For example, two different inducers each activate half of a split transcription factor. Only when both halves are present do they combine to activate the output gene. Without both signals, nothing happens.

faq.question: What practical applications could biological logic gates enable?
faq.answer: Engineered immune cells that kill only cells displaying two specific cancer markers, reducing damage to healthy tissue. Environmental bacteria that produce cleanup enzymes only when detecting both a pollutant and sufficient nutrients. Agricultural microbes responding to specific soil conditions.
